title: Identity-related Speech Suppression in Generative AI Content Moderation
findings: Non-Christian content was found to be significantly more likely to be incorrectly suppressed across all tested content moderation APIs compared to Christian content and non-identity-related content. This suppression was often due to being flagged as 'hateful' or 'violent'. For instance, the Google API specifically flagged non-Christian content under its 'Religion & Belief' category. This pattern was consistent and had a notably high effect size in regression analyses.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures 'speech suppression,' defined as the rate at which appropriate text related to specific identity groups is incorrectly flagged as violating content moderation policies. For faith/religion, it specifically measures whether 'Christian' and 'non-Christian' content is disproportionately suppressed, often by being flagged as violent or hateful.
